    "summary": "GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter",
    "description": "## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

# gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

# gh-380 rework — fix CI red head on PR #381

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red CI head (`9c452441`)** — a transport-parity flake in
  the new `gitlab_list_project_jobs` tool, reproduced locally against the exact
  CI shard (`dart test --total-shards 4 --shard-index 1`):

  ```text
  ❌ gitlab_list_project_jobs maps scope to repeated scope[] params
  Expected: contains 'scope%5B%5D=success'
  Actual:   '/api/v4/projects/g%2Fr/jobs?per_page=20&page=1&scope[]=success'
  ```

  `SyncHttpClient` has two transports with **different wire behavior for
  non-ASCII URL bytes**: the curl fallback sends the URL string verbatim

  `Uri.parse`/`HttpClient`, which percent-encodes to `scope%5B%5D=`. The tool

  "key": "gh-380",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter",
    "description": "## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

# gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

  "key": "gh-380",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter",
    "description": "## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

# gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

# gh-380 rework — fix CI red head on PR #381

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red CI head (`9c452441`)** — a transport-parity flake in
  the new `gitlab_list_project_jobs` tool, reproduced locally against the exact
  CI shard (`dart test --total-shards 4 --shard-index 1`):

  ```text
  ❌ gitlab_list_project_jobs maps scope to repeated scope[] params
  Expected: contains 'scope%5B%5D=success'
  Actual:   '/api/v4/projects/g%2Fr/jobs?per_page=20&page=1&scope[]=success'
  ```

  `SyncHttpClient` has two transports with **different wire behavior for
  non-ASCII URL bytes**: the curl fallback sends the URL string verbatim
  (literal `scope[]=`), while the pooled-isolate bridge routes it through
  `Uri.parse`/`HttpClient`, which percent-encodes to `scope%5B%5D=`. The tool
  built the query with literal brackets and relied on the bridge to encode
  them; whether the bridge or curl serves a request is a `SyncHttpBridge`
  boot-timing race that flips with machine load — green in isolated runs,
  red under the full sharded suite. Verified empirically against a local
  echo server: curl logs `scope[]=success`, Dart `HttpClient` logs
  `scope%5B%5D=success` for the same URL.
- The other red checks (`gate`, `agents-gate`) are downstream merge jobs of
  the failed shards; `static` (format+analyze) passes locally on this head
  and its CI log was not included in the input, so no in-tree cause was
  found — the flake fix plus a fresh head re-arms validation.
- No open PR review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `{"threads": []}`);
  review decision `NONE`.

## Approach

TDD, one finding:

1. **RED** — added a deterministic regression test
   (`scope[] params are wire-identical on both HTTP transports`) that forces
   each transport in turn — `SyncHttpBridge.shared.dispose()` before the sync
   call guarantees the curl fallback, `await SyncHttpBridge.shared.boot()`
   guarantees the isolate bridge — and pins the echo-server-logged path to
   the percent-encoded form on both. Failed pre-fix with the literal
   `scope[]=` wire bytes (the exact CI failure).
2. **GREEN** — `_listProjectJobs` now pre-encodes the param name:
   `scope%5B%5D=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}`. Both transports emit
   identical bytes (`Uri.parse` keeps valid escapes, no double-encoding —
   the pre-existing `%2F` project path confirms). GitLab decodes
   `scope%5B%5D` identically to `scope[]`.
3. **REFACTOR** — moved the new test into its own `testjoblisttools_p5()`
   group: placing it in `p2` pushed that function to 71 lines and failed the
   `method_size` gate (max 60), the same reason the file was originally
   split p1–p4. Doc comment on `_listProjectJobs` now records the
   wire-parity invariant.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/gitlab_sync_tools.dart` — `_listProjectJobs` emits
  `scope%5B%5D=` instead of literal `scope[]=`, with a comment explaining
  the two-transport invariant (gh-380).
- `test/js/sync_tools/gitlab_job_list_tools_test.dart` — new transport-parity
  regression test in a dedicated `testjoblisttools_p5()` group (keeps every
  group function under the 60-line `method_size` gate).

Commits on `ai/gh-380` (pushed, new head for validation):

- `d63d517c` (auto-save) — scope[] pre-encoding + regression test
- `c01b8c63` — p5 group split (method_size gate)

## Test Coverage

- New regression test exercises both transports deterministically
  (dispose→curl, await-boot→bridge) — the previously racy assertion can no
  longer flip with load.
- Full suite, CI-identical sharding (Dart 3.13.5, QuickJS built locally):
  - shard 0: **1015 passed**
  - shard 1 (the red one): **1006 passed, 12 skipped**
  - shard 2: **955 passed, 1 skipped**
  - shard 3: **948 passed, 3 skipped**
  - total **3924 passed** (PR baseline 3923 + 1 new regression test), 0 failed
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` — clean; `dart analyze` — no issues.
- `crap4dart check --all` — 19 passed / 1 failed locally where the single
  failure is `test_coverage` (no `coverage/lcov.info` exists outside CI;
  CI's `test` shards generate it and `gate` merges it — full local
  `dart test --coverage` run launched to confirm); `method_size` violation
  introduced mid-rework was fixed by the p5 split. `crap4dart analyze` —
  Max CRAP 0.00, threshold 8.00 OK.
- E2E (AC1–AC3) still requires live GitLab credentials — not runnable in
  this sandbox (unchanged from the PR's original note).

  "key": "gh-380",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter",
    "description": "## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

# gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

# gh-380 rework — fix CI red head on PR #381

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red CI head (`9c452441`)** — a transport-parity flake in
  the new `gitlab_list_project_jobs` tool, reproduced locally against the exact
  CI shard (`dart test --total-shards 4 --shard-index 1`):

  ```text
  ❌ gitlab_list_project_jobs maps scope to repeated scope[] params
  Expected: contains 'scope%5B%5D=success'
  Actual:   '/api/v4/projects/g%2Fr/jobs?per_page=20&page=1&scope[]=success'
  ```

  `SyncHttpClient` has two transports with **different wire behavior for
  non-ASCII URL bytes**: the curl fallback sends the URL string verbatim
  (literal `scope[]=`), while the pooled-isolate bridge routes it through
  `Uri.parse`/`HttpClient`, which percent-encodes to `scope%5B%5D=`. The tool
  built the query with literal brackets and relied on the bridge to encode
  them; whether the bridge or curl serves a request is a `SyncHttpBridge`
  boot-timing race that flips with machine load — green in isolated runs,
  red under the full sharded suite. Verified empirically against a local
  echo server: curl logs `scope[]=success`, Dart `HttpClient` logs
  `scope%5B%5D=success` for the same URL.
- The other red checks (`gate`, `agents-gate`) are downstream merge jobs of
  the failed shards; `static` (format+analyze) passes locally on this head
  and its CI log was not included in the input, so no in-tree cause was
  found — the flake fix plus a fresh head re-arms validation.
- No open PR review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `{"threads": []}`);
  review decision `NONE`.

## Approach

TDD, one finding:

1. **RED** — added a deterministic regression test
   (`scope[] params are wire-identical on both HTTP transports`) that forces
   each transport in turn — `SyncHttpBridge.shared.dispose()` before the sync
   call guarantees the curl fallback, `await SyncHttpBridge.shared.boot()`
   guarantees the isolate bridge — and pins the echo-server-logged path to
   the percent-encoded form on both. Failed pre-fix with the literal
   `scope[]=` wire bytes (the exact CI failure).
2. **GREEN** — `_listProjectJobs` now pre-encodes the param name:
   `scope%5B%5D=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}`. Both transports emit
   identical bytes (`Uri.parse` keeps valid escapes, no double-encoding —
   the pre-existing `%2F` project path confirms). GitLab decodes
   `scope%5B%5D` identically to `scope[]`.
3. **REFACTOR** — moved the new test into its own `testjoblisttools_p5()`
   group: placing it in `p2` pushed that function to 71 lines and failed the
   `method_size` gate (max 60), the same reason the file was originally
   split p1–p4. Doc comment on `_listProjectJobs` now records the
   wire-parity invariant.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-380` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +553
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T19:30:21Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T20:16:15Z

## PR Description

Closes #380
### What changed
Added `gitlab_list_project_jobs` as a first-class GitLab tool: sync executor in `GitLabSyncTools` (project-wide `GET projects/{id}/jobs`, or pipeline-scoped `…/pipelines/{pid}/jobs` via `pipelineId`) with client-side exact-name filter (GitLab has no server-side one), `scope[]` mapping, and `per_page` (max 100 clamp)/`page` handling — plus a registry definition so agent scripts get a real JS wrapper. Closed the phantom-name trap (AC5): implemented sync executors for `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline`, dropped the five declared-but-unrouted rows from `kGitlabRequiredParams`, and added a catalog/runtime coherence test that fails on any `gitlab_*` name the runtime rejects.

### Key decisions
- Java spec pinned from `dm.ai GitLab.java`: `listJobs(workspace, repository)` and `getPipelineJobs(workspace, repository, pipelineId)`; the gh-380 extensions (`name`, `scope`, `per_page`, `page`, `pipelineId`) are optional params, so `gitlab_list_project_jobs` lands in `java_mcp_param_drift.txt`, not parity.
- Bare-array return (unwrapList-style) mirroring `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`; empty name match returns `[]`, never an error.
- Dropped phantom rows (`gitlab_cancel_job`, `gitlab_delete_release_asset`, `gitlab_get_mr_activities`, `gitlab_get_pipeline_jobs`, `gitlab_list_release_assets`) instead of implementing — they stay tracked in `java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` and regain a row when ported.
- `scm_ci`'s `ci_get_verdict` GitLab runId gap left untouched (out of scope; pinned tests keep the honest-gap error).

# gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

# gh-380 rework — fix CI red head on PR #381

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red CI head (`9c452441`)** — a transport-parity flake in
  the new `gitlab_list_project_jobs` tool, reproduced locally against the exact
  CI shard (`dart test --total-shards 4 --shard-index 1`):

  ```text
  ❌ gitlab_list_project_jobs maps scope to repeated scope[] params
  Expected: contains 'scope%5B%5D=success'
  Actual:   '/api/v4/projects/g%2Fr/jobs?per_page=20&page=1&scope[]=success'
  ```

  `SyncHttpClient` has two transports with **different wire behavior for
  non-ASCII URL bytes**: the curl fallback sends the URL string verbatim
  (literal `scope[]=`), while the pooled-isolate bridge routes it through
  `Uri.parse`/`HttpClient`, which percent-encodes to `scope%5B%5D=`. The tool
  built the query with literal brackets and relied on the bridge to encode
  them; whether the bridge or curl serves a request is a `SyncHttpBridge`
  boot-timing race that flips with machine load — green in isolated runs,
  red under the full sharded suite. Verified empirically against a local
  echo server: curl logs `scope[]=success`, Dart `HttpClient` logs
  `scope%5B%5D=success` for the same URL.
- The other red checks (`gate`, `agents-gate`) are downstream merge jobs of
  the failed shards; `static` (format+analyze) passes locally on this head
  and its CI log was not included in the input, so no in-tree cause was
  found — the flake fix plus a fresh head re-arms validation.
- No open PR review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `{"threads": []}`);
  review decision `NONE`.

## Approach

TDD, one finding:

1. **RED** — added a deterministic regression test
   (`scope[] params are wire-identical on both HTTP transports`) that forces
   each transport in turn — `SyncHttpBridge.shared.dispose()` before the sync
   call guarantees the curl fallback, `await SyncHttpBridge.shared.boot()`
   guarantees the isolate bridge — and pins the echo-server-logged path to
   the percent-encoded form on both. Failed pre-fix with the literal
   `scope[]=` wire bytes (the exact CI failure).
2. **GREEN** — `_listProjectJobs` now pre-encodes the param name:
   `scope%5B%5D=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}`. Both transports emit
   identical bytes (`Uri.parse` keeps valid escapes, no double-encoding —
   the pre-existing `%2F` project path confirms). GitLab decodes
   `scope%5B%5D` identically to `scope[]`.
3. **REFACTOR** — moved the new test into its own `testjoblisttools_p5()`
   group: placing it in `p2` pushed that function to 71 lines and failed the
   `method_size` gate (max 60), the same reason the file was originally
   split p1–p4. Doc comment on `_listProjectJobs` now records the
   wire-parity invariant.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/gitlab_sync_tools.dart` — `_listProjectJobs` emits
  `scope%5B%5D=` instead of literal `scope[]=`, with a comment explaining
  the two-transport invariant (gh-380).
- `test/js/sync_tools/gitlab_job_list_tools_test.dart` — new transport-parity
  regression test in a dedicated `testjoblisttools_p5()` group (keeps every
  group function under the 60-line `method_size` gate).

Commits on `ai/gh-380` (pushed, new head for validation):

- `d63d517c` (auto-save) — scope[] pre-encoding + regression test
- `c01b8c63` — p5 group split (method_size gate)

## Test Coverage

- New regression test exercises both transports deterministically
  (dispose→curl, await-boot→bridge) — the previously racy assertion can no
  longer flip with load.
- Full suite, CI-identical sharding (Dart 3.13.5, QuickJS built locally):
  - shard 0: **1015 passed**
  - shard 1 (the red one): **1006 passed, 12 skipped**
  - shard 2: **955 passed, 1 skipped**
  - shard 3: **948 passed, 3 skipped**
  - total **3924 passed** (PR baseline 3923 + 1 new regression test), 0 failed
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` — clean; `dart analyze` — no issues.
- `crap4dart check --all` — 19 passed / 1 failed locally where the single
  failure is `test_coverage` (no `coverage/lcov.info` exists outside CI;
  CI's `test` shards generate it and `gate` merges it — full local
  `dart test --coverage` run launched to confirm); `method_size` violation
  introduced mid-rework was fixed by the p5 split. `crap4dart analyze` —
  Max CRAP 0.00, threshold 8.00 OK.
- E2E (AC1–AC3) still requires live GitLab credentials — not runnable in
  this sandbox (unchanged from the PR's original note).

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Closes #380
### What changed
Added `gitlab_list_project_jobs` as a first-class GitLab tool: sync executor in `GitLabSyncTools` (project-wide `GET projects/{id}/jobs`, or pipeline-scoped `…/pipelines/{pid}/jobs` via `pipelineId`) with client-side exact-name filter (GitLab has no server-side one), `scope[]` mapping, and `per_page` (max 100 clamp)/`page` handling — plus a registry definition so agent scripts get a real JS wrapper. # gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-rework) · [run](https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/actions/runs/38080879916) · started 19:43 · done 19:58 ✅

# gh-380 rework — fix CI red head on PR #381

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red CI head (`9c452441`)** — a transport-parity flake in
  the new `gitlab_list_project_jobs` tool, reproduced locally against the exact
  CI shard (`dart test --total-shards 4 --shard-index 1`):

  ```text
  ❌ gitlab_list_project_jobs maps scope to repeated scope[] params
  Expected: contains 'scope%5B%5D=success'
  Actual:   '/api/v4/projects/g%2Fr/jobs?per_page=20&page=1&scope[]=success'
  ```

  `SyncHttpClient` has two transports with **different wire behavior for
  non-ASCII URL bytes**: the curl fallback sends the URL string verbatim
  (literal `scope[]=`), while the pooled-isolate bridge routes it through
  `Uri.parse`/`HttpClient`, which percent-encodes to `scope%5B%5D=`. The tool
  built the query with literal brackets and relied on the bridge to encode
  them; whether the bridge or curl serves a request is a `SyncHttpBridge`
  boot-timing race that flips with machine load — green in isolated runs,
  red under the full sharded suite. Verified empirically against a local
  echo server: curl logs `scope[]=success`, Dart `HttpClient` logs
  `scope%5B%5D=success` for the same URL.
- The other red checks (`gate`, `agents-gate`) are downstream merge jobs of
  the failed shards; `static` (format+analyze) passes locally on this head
  and its CI log was not included in the input, so no in-tree cause was
  found — the flake fix plus a fresh head re-arms validation.
- No open PR review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `{"threads": []}`);
  review decision `NONE`.

## Approach

TDD, one finding:

1. **RED** — added a deterministic regression test
   (`scope[] params are wire-identical on both HTTP transports`) that forces
   each transport in turn — `SyncHttpBridge.shared.dispose()` before the sync
   call guarantees the curl fallback, `await SyncHttpBridge.shared.boot()`
   guarantees the isolate bridge — and pins the echo-server-logged path to
   the percent-encoded form on both. Failed pre-fix with the literal
   `scope[]=` wire bytes (the exact CI failure).
2. **GREEN** — `_listProjectJobs` now pre-encodes the param name:
   `scope%5B%5D=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}`. Both transports emit
   identical bytes (`Uri.parse` keeps valid escapes, no double-encoding —
   the pre-existing `%2F` project path confirms). GitLab decodes
   `scope%5B%5D` identically to `scope[]`.
3. **REFACTOR** — moved the new test into its own `testjoblisttools_p5()`
   group: placing it in `p2` pushed that function to 71 lines and failed the
   `method_size` gate (max 60), the same reason the file was originally
   split p1–p4. Doc comment on `_listProjectJobs` now records the
   wire-parity invariant.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/gitlab_sync_tools.dart` — `_listProjectJobs` emits
  `scope%5B%5D=` instead of literal `scope[]=`, with a comment explaining
  the two-transport invariant (gh-380).
- `test/js/sync_tools/gitlab_job_list_tools_test.dart` — new transport-parity
  regression test in a dedicated `testjoblisttools_p5()` group (keeps every
  group function under the 60-line `method_size` gate).

Commits on `ai/gh-380` (pushed, new head for validation):

- `d63d517c` (auto-save) — scope[] pre-encoding + regression test
- `c01b8c63` — p5 group split (method_size gate)

## Test Coverage

- New regression test exercises both transports deterministically
  (dispose→curl, await-boot→bridge) — the previously racy assertion can no
  longer flip with load.
- Full suite, CI-identical sharding (Dart 3.13.5, QuickJS built locally):
  - shard 0: **1015 passed**
  - shard 1 (the red one): **1006 passed, 12 skipped**
  - shard 2: **955 passed, 1 skipped**
  - shard 3: **948 passed, 3 skipped**
  - total **3924 passed** (PR baseline 3923 + 1 new regression test), 0 failed
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` — clean; `dart analyze` — no issues.
- `crap4dart check --all` — 19 passed / 1 failed locally where the single
  failure is `test_coverage` (no `coverage/lcov.info` exists outside CI;
  CI's `test` shards generate it and `gate` merges it — full local
  `dart test --coverage` run launched to confirm); `method_size` violation
  introduced mid-rework was fixed by the p5 split. `crap4dart analyze` —
  Max CRAP 0.00, threshold 8.00 OK.
- E2E (AC1–AC3) still requires live GitLab credentials — not runnable in
  this sandbox (unchanged from the PR's original note).

Added `gitlab_list_project_jobs` as a first-class GitLab tool: sync executor in `GitLabSyncTools` (project-wide `GET projects/{id}/jobs`, or pipeline-scoped `…/pipelines/{pid}/jobs` via `pipelineId`) with client-side exact-name filter (GitLab has no server-side one), `scope[]` mapping, and `per_page` (max 100 clamp)/`page` handling — plus a registry definition so agent scripts get a real JS wrapper. # gh-380: GitLab: add jobs listing tool (project + pipeline scope) with exact-name filter

## Description

## Goal — Jobs listing becomes a first-class dmtools GitLab tool (v1)
One sentence: **an agent config can discover CI jobs (project-wide or per-pipeline) and filter them by exact name, without leaving the dmtools sandbox.**

Today the only job-level GitLab tool is `gitlab_get_job_logs(jobId)` — it requires a job id nobody can obtain in-sandbox. There is no project-jobs or pipeline-jobs listing tool: probed exhaustively on dmtools 0.1.43/0.1.44 (26 live `gitlab_*` tools; none list jobs). Consequence in our factory (ai-teammate-runner): every job-id consumer is forced into a bash-layer curl collector outside agents — token telemetry (CM-3626), job dashboards, failure reports. Worse, the tool CATALOG lists names the runtime rejects (`gitlab_get_pipelines`, `gitlab_get_pipeline` -> "Unsupported GitLab tool"), which invited a real bug: our dev agent wrote code against a plausible catalog name (`gitlab_list_project_jobs`) that does not exist anywhere; unit mocks stubbed it and the failure surfaced only in production.

## Why this framing
- The need is LIST + FILTER (discover ids by name), not trace reading (exists) and not pipeline listing (exists as `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`).
- The name filter must live in the tool even though GitLab has no server-side filter: the caller's contract is "give me the ai-teammate jobs", not "give me 100 jobs and good luck".

## Platform facts (GitLab REST v4 — pin, do not assume)
- `GET /projects/:id/jobs` — params: `scope[]`, `per_page` (max 100), `page`; **no server-side name filter exists** (verify at implementation time; if upstream adds one, pass through).
- `GET /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/jobs` — same job object shape, pipeline-scoped. This is the shape consumers need most (a dispatch pipeline is short-lived; "its jobs" is the natural query).
- Job object fields consumers rely on: `id`, `name`, `status`, `stage`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration`, `web_url`, `pipeline.id`, `runner.description`.
- Pagination is page-based only (no cursor); order is newest-first by default.

## Capability surface
| API | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/projects/:id/jobs` | `gitlab_list_project_jobs(workspace, repository, {name?, scope?, per_page?, page?})` | project-wide, newest-first |
| `/projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs` | same tool with `pipelineId` param | pipeline-scoped variant (preferred shape) |
| name filter | client-side exact match inside the tool | documented as client-side; empty result is a valid result |
| catalog/runtime coherence | drop or implement the phantom `gitlab_get_pipelines`/`gitlab_get_pipeline` catalog entries | a catalog name that the integration rejects is a trap, see incident above |

Conventions to mirror: `workspace`/`repository` split, `unwrapList`-style array return, error shape of `gitlab_list_pipeline_runs`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `gitlab_list_project_jobs` with `pipelineId` returns the real job ids of that pipeline (live E2E against a pipeline with a known single job).
- **AC2** — `name: "ai-teammate"` narrows the result to jobs with exactly that name; a name with no matches returns an empty list, not an error.
- **AC3** — without `pipelineId`, returns the project's latest jobs honoring `per_page`/`page` (max 100 clamp).
- **AC4** — `scope[]` maps to the API param (e.g. `success`, `running`).
- **AC5** — the tool catalog contains no `gitlab_*` name that the runtime rejects (a coherence check/test).

## Test plan
- `UT-*` param building, name filter, pagination clamp, empty-name handling.
- `IT-*` fake transport: job array shapes, pipeline-scoped vs project-wide paths.
- `E2E-*` live GitLab: single-job dispatch pipeline (AC1), name filter (AC2), multi-page project query (AC3).
- `REG-*` existing gitlab tool suite stays green; catalog coherence test (AC5) runs in CI and blocks merge on a phantom name.

## Non-goals
- Trace/log fetching (`gitlab_get_job_logs` exists).
- GitHub Actions job listing.
- Retry/backoff policies (transport layer concern).

## Open questions
- Naming: `gitlab_list_project_jobs` vs `gitlab_list_jobs` (we already reference the former in consumer code — a phantom call today, a working call the day this lands).
- Should `common/scm.js`'s GitLab provider gain `listJobs` alongside `listWorkflowRuns` for parity?

## References
- Incident: ai-teammate-runner CM-3626 — publisher called the (then nonexistent) `gitlab_list_project_jobs`; mocks hid it; live run surfaced it.
- Tool inventory probe 2026-10-10: 47 catalog gitlab names, 26 live, zero job-listing.

- [x] ▶ dev (fa-rework) · [run](https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/actions/runs/38080879916) · started 19:43 · done 19:58 ✅

# gh-380 rework — fix CI red head on PR #381

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red CI head (`9c452441`)** — a transport-parity flake in
  the new `gitlab_list_project_jobs` tool, reproduced locally against the exact
  CI shard (`dart test --total-shards 4 --shard-index 1`):

  ```text
  ❌ gitlab_list_project_jobs maps scope to repeated scope[] params
  Expected: contains 'scope%5B%5D=success'
  Actual:   '/api/v4/projects/g%2Fr/jobs?per_page=20&page=1&scope[]=success'
  ```

  `SyncHttpClient` has two transports with **different wire behavior for
  non-ASCII URL bytes**: the curl fallback sends the URL string verbatim
  (literal `scope[]=`), while the pooled-isolate bridge routes it through
  `Uri.parse`/`HttpClient`, which percent-encodes to `scope%5B%5D=`. The tool
  built the query with literal brackets and relied on the bridge to encode
  them; whether the bridge or curl serves a request is a `SyncHttpBridge`
  boot-timing race that flips with machine load — green in isolated runs,
  red under the full sharded suite. Verified empirically against a local
  echo server: curl logs `scope[]=success`, Dart `HttpClient` logs
  `scope%5B%5D=success` for the same URL.
- The other red checks (`gate`, `agents-gate`) are downstream merge jobs of
  the failed shards; `static` (format+analyze) passes locally on this head
  and its CI log was not included in the input, so no in-tree cause was
  found — the flake fix plus a fresh head re-arms validation.
- No open PR review threads (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `{"threads": []}`);
  review decision `NONE`.

## Approach

TDD, one finding:

1. **RED** — added a deterministic regression test
   (`scope[] params are wire-identical on both HTTP transports`) that forces
   each transport in turn — `SyncHttpBridge.shared.dispose()` before the sync
   call guarantees the curl fallback, `await SyncHttpBridge.shared.boot()`
   guarantees the isolate bridge — and pins the echo-server-logged path to
   the percent-encoded form on both. Failed pre-fix with the literal
   `scope[]=` wire bytes (the exact CI failure).
2. **GREEN** — `_listProjectJobs` now pre-encodes the param name:
   `scope%5B%5D=${Uri.encodeQueryComponent(scope)}`. Both transports emit
   identical bytes (`Uri.parse` keeps valid escapes, no double-encoding —
   the pre-existing `%2F` project path confirms). GitLab decodes
   `scope%5B%5D` identically to `scope[]`.
3. **REFACTOR** — moved the new test into its own `testjoblisttools_p5()`
   group: placing it in `p2` pushed that function to 71 lines and failed the
   `method_size` gate (max 60), the same reason the file was originally
   split p1–p4. Doc comment on `_listProjectJobs` now records the
   wire-parity invariant.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/js/sync_tools/gitlab_sync_tools.dart` — `_listProjectJobs` emits
  `scope%5B%5D=` instead of literal `scope[]=`, with a comment explaining
  the two-transport invariant (gh-380).
- `test/js/sync_tools/gitlab_job_list_tools_test.dart` — new transport-parity
  regression test in a dedicated `testjoblisttools_p5()` group (keeps every
  group function under the 60-line `method_size` gate).

Commits on `ai/gh-380` (pushed, new head for validation):

- `d63d517c` (auto-save) — scope[] pre-encoding + regression test
- `c01b8c63` — p5 group split (method_size gate)

## Test Coverage

- New regression test exercises both transports deterministically
  (dispose→curl, await-boot→bridge) — the previously racy assertion can no
  longer flip with load.
- Full suite, CI-identical sharding (Dart 3.13.5, QuickJS built locally):
  - shard 0: **1015 passed**
  - shard 1 (the red one): **1006 passed, 12 skipped**
  - shard 2: **955 passed, 1 skipped**
  - shard 3: **948 passed, 3 skipped**
  - total **3924 passed** (PR baseline 3923 + 1 new regression test), 0 failed
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` — clean; `dart analyze` — no issues.
- `crap4dart check --all` — 19 passed / 1 failed locally where the single
  failure is `test_coverage` (no `coverage/lcov.info` exists outside CI;
  CI's `test` shards generate it and `gate` merges it — full local
  `dart test --coverage` run launched to confirm); `method_size` violation
  introduced mid-rework was fixed by the p5 split. `crap4dart analyze` —
  Max CRAP 0.00, threshold 8.00 OK.
- E2E (AC1–AC3) still requires live GitLab credentials — not runnable in
  this sandbox (unchanged from the PR's original note).
